cli.usage:
usage: mcp-n4 [-h] [--allow-writes] [--write-scope ORD_PREFIX]
              [--state-dir STATE_DIR] [--token-ttl SECONDS] [--max-writes N]
              [--auth-cooldown SECONDS] [--load-wait SECONDS]
              [--http-timeout SECONDS] [--station NAME=URL]
              [--station-home NAME=PATH] [--credential-env PREFIX]
              [--insecure-tls NAME] [--allow-tier-b NAME]
              [--allow-tier-c NAME] [--progress-file PATH]
              [--allow-http-for-tests]
cli.help:
usage: mcp-n4 [-h] [--allow-writes] [--write-scope ORD_PREFIX]
              [--state-dir STATE_DIR] [--token-ttl SECONDS] [--max-writes N]
              [--auth-cooldown SECONDS] [--load-wait SECONDS]
              [--http-timeout SECONDS] [--station NAME=URL]
              [--station-home NAME=PATH] [--credential-env PREFIX]
              [--insecure-tls NAME] [--allow-tier-b NAME]
              [--allow-tier-c NAME] [--progress-file PATH]
              [--allow-http-for-tests]

Stdio MCP server for Niagara N4 stations (newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0). Run
the `mcp-n4` binary: starting it prints nothing and contacts no station. MCP
protocol versions: this server speaks 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05
(`server.protocol_versions` of the registry). A client asking for a newer
revision is answered with 2025-06-18. Only add a newer revision to that list
once its semantics (new message shapes, capabilities, required fields) are
implemented and tested here.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --allow-writes        register the write tools (dry run + confirmation token
                        each)
  --write-scope ORD_PREFIX
                        ORD prefix writes may touch (repeatable); none = no
                        writes
  --state-dir STATE_DIR
                        journal/audit directory (default
                        ~/.local/state/mcp-n4)
  --token-ttl SECONDS   confirmation token lifetime (default 300)
  --max-writes N        executed writes allowed per server process (default
                        200); a reconnect does not reset it
  --auth-cooldown SECONDS
                        after an authentication failure, refuse station calls
                        this long (default and minimum 30: the lock-out
                        window)
  --load-wait SECONDS   total wait for one component load (default 3; 1-60):
                        raise it for a slow or remote station
  --http-timeout SECONDS
                        HTTP timeout of one station request (default 20;
                        5-300)
  --station NAME=URL    station n4_connect may use (repeatable); NAME should
                        equal the station's stationName; URL must be https://
  --station-home NAME=PATH
                        directory holding the config.bog of configured station
                        NAME; lets n4_save_station prove persistence
                        (repeatable)
  --credential-env PREFIX
                        env var prefix holding <PREFIX>_USER/<PREFIX>_PASSWORD
                        (default MCP_N4)
  --insecure-tls NAME   skip TLS certificate verification for this configured
                        station (self-signed); repeatable
  --allow-tier-b NAME   let writes run on configured station NAME although its
                        version is tier B (4.15/4.3); only after a PoC matched
                        that build (METHODOLOGY section 5); repeatable
  --allow-tier-c NAME   let writes run on configured station NAME although its
                        version is tier C (other or unknown); only after
                        reg.loadContract, loadRoot and a harmless scratch
                        write succeeded; repeatable
  --progress-file PATH  append JSON progress lines of long reads
                        (n4_inventory) to PATH
  --allow-http-for-tests
                        permit http:// base URLs (fake station in tests only)

read_tools.name: n4_connect
read_tools.description: Open a session to one of the stations the operator configured at server start (replaces any previous session). The URL, credentials and TLS policy are fixed by the operator and cannot be chosen here. The station's real stationName must equal expected_station (default: the configured station NAME), or the session is closed. Reports the detected version (oBIX productVersion) and its tier: A (4.13/4.14) writes; B (4.15/4.3) and C (other or unknown) refuse writes unless the operator opted the station in.

expected_station.description: Required stationName; default: the station NAME

read_tools.name: n4_describe_session
read_tools.description: Report whether a station session is active, which station, its version tier, and the server mode. Works without a session.

read_tools.name: n4_navigate
read_tools.description: List the children of a component (name, type, handle, has_children). depth > 1 nests grandchildren under a 'children' key. elapsed_ms is the load time. For a station inventory use n4_bql_query or n4_inventory instead: one navigate is one round trip per component. types (optional) keeps only children whose type is one of the given specs (e.g. bacnet:BacnetDevice) plus the path to them; each kept entry then carries matched true/false. has_children ignores the types filter: it is true when the entry has any component child, matching or not. types keeps a given type and its subtypes; types_note says when the registry could not be read.

types.description: Optional type specs to keep, e.g. ['bacnet:BacnetDevice']; default: no filter

read_tools.name: n4_read_slots
read_tools.description: Read all slots of one component as {name, type, value, status}. Status complexes add status_ok/status_null; omitted values take the type default. value_display carries the station's display string; a complex the reader cannot decode (e.g. a Modbus FlexAddress) returns that display string as value. elapsed_ms is the load time. A slot that is itself a baja:Status also adds status_flags, the names of the flags set; status_ok is false when any is set.

read_tools.name: n4_list_links
read_tools.description: List baja:Link / baja:ConversionLink links of components up to depth levels below ord. source_path is null when the source handle is outside the loaded subtree.

depth.description: Component levels below ord to scan (1-4)

read_tools.name: n4_find_dangling_outputs
read_tools.description: List components (up to depth levels below ord) with an 'out' slot that no link in the subtree uses as a source. Links from outside the subtree are not seen. A source ORD that is neither a handle nor an absolute slot path cannot be resolved: outputs it may feed are listed as unknown, not dangling.

depth.description: Component levels below ord to scan (1-4)

read_tools.name: n4_bql_query
read_tools.description: Bulk read: one projected BQL select over a subtree, returned as rows (one HTTP GET, usually under a second, where a navigate crawl costs one round trip per component). Use it FIRST for any inventory. Only 'select <cols> from <type> [where ...]' is accepted; '|' is refused. Columns are the station's display headers (e.g. 'Slot Path', 'Name'; a localized station translates them, a repeated header becomes 'Type#2'); the queried name column is decoded ($20 -> space), 'Slot Path' stays ORD-ready. Proxy-extension fields project as proxyExt.<slot>, e.g. proxyExt.dataAddress. Rows are capped (truncated=true when cut).

base.description: Subtree ORD or slot path, e.g. station:|slot:/Drivers (default: the station root)

query.description: select <columns> from <type> [where ...], e.g. select slotPath, name, out from control:ControlPoint

output_file.description: Optional plain file name (.csv or .json): the rows go to <state-dir>/bql/<name> (0600, never overwritten) instead of the reply

read_tools.name: n4_inventory
read_tools.description: Station inventory through three BQL queries: networks, devices and points below base (default /Drivers), counted per network and per device. A network's built-in local device slot (localDevice, e.g. SnmpNetwork's own agent) is flagged local=true and counted apart from field devices. progress lists each step's row count; the operator's --progress-file gets the same lines. A network is a driver:DeviceNetwork row at any depth, named by its path below base.

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per query in seconds

read_tools.name: n4_read_file
read_tools.description: Read one station file (e.g. a Px view file:^px/General.px) through the station's file servlet: GET /file/<path>. file_ord is a file:^ ORD or a path relative to the station home. Refused before any request: '..', '|', ':', absolute paths, directories, names ending in '.' or ' ' and .bog/.bog.gz (the station never serves them). Text types (px, xml, nav, chart, json, csv, html, txt, ...) return text; other files return size, sha256 and content type only (output_file saves the complete bytes under <state-dir>/files/). status is ok, forbidden (403: no read permission) or not_found (404); a 401 pauses station calls and is never retried. Reads are capped at max_bytes (truncated=true, sha256 null when cut).

output_file.description: Optional plain file name with an extension: the complete bytes go to <state-dir>/files/<name> (0600, never overwritten)

read_tools.name: n4_list_px_views
read_tools.description: List the Px views (baja:PxView) below root with one BQL query: display_name, px_file (the file:^ ORD to pass to n4_read_file / n4_px_summary) and media. A PxView is a property value, not a component, so the station usually answers its slot path as NULL: slot_path and owner_path are null then (see owner_note).

read_tools.name: n4_px_summary
read_tools.description: Fetch one .px file (like n4_read_file) and summarize it without returning the XML: media, imported modules, canvases and viewSize, layers, widget and binding type counts, bound ORDs grouped by component (a trailing value slot such as /out stripped), images, included Px files, charts, other ORDs and label texts. Every list is capped at max_items. A file larger than max_bytes is refused, not summarized in part.

read_tools.name: n4_list_batches
read_tools.description: List the write batches in this server's journal, newest first: batch_id, tool, station_name, ts, state (completed / in-doubt), verdict, rollback_of and rolled_back_by. Use it to find the batch_id for n4_rollback. A journal line that cannot be read is listed in unreadable and the reply says the list is incomplete. Reads the journal only; works without a session.

read_tools.name: n4_session_retro_draft
read_tools.description: Draft the session retro: reads this server's audit and journal and returns markdown plus evidence-backed CANDIDATE kit deltas (refusals, bad read-back verdicts, in-doubt batches, BOX errors, dangling outputs). Proposes only; never applies or stages anything. An audit line that cannot be read is named in the summary, which says the draft is incomplete. The window starts at the server start; pass since (ISO-8601, e.g. 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z for the whole history) to change it.

since.description: ISO-8601 timestamp; only newer entries are considered (default: when this server started)

read_tools.name: n4_spy_page
read_tools.description: Read one diagnostics page of the station's spy tree (GET /ord?spy:/<path>, the pages the Workbench Spy view shows) as data: title, tables (title, header, rows of cells), links to child pages as relative spy paths, the POST actions the page offers (named only as spy paths without their query, never invoked) and the text outside tables. The content of a form field (textarea, select, button, input) is never returned, wherever it sits. Read-only: one GET under the spy root. Refused before any request: a scheme or ':' , '|', '..', a query string ('?', '&', '=', '#'), '%', ';', a backslash, any Unicode control character, invalid UTF-8 and the known action pages (util/gc, util/forceThreadDump). status is ok, forbidden (the user may not read spy pages), not_found, not_html or parse_timeout (the page was not parsed within timeout_s). Spy pages are diagnostics: their layout differs between Niagara versions, so read the tables as found. The reply is bounded as a whole: truncated is true when a cap cut it and truncated_by names the caps (max_bytes, max_rows across all tables, tables, row_cells, links, actions, name, cell, text).

path.description: Path below the spy root, e.g. metrics, sysInfo or util/JMX Info; empty for the index

max_rows.description: Cap of table rows returned, all tables together

max_bytes.description: Byte cap of the page read

read_tools.name: n4_station_health
read_tools.description: Station health in one call, each section answered on its own: system (the SystemService slots by their station names: CPU usage in percent, memory as the station reports it plus memory_used_percent, version, host, time), points (total, ok, null_only, not_ok_count, a count per status flag in by_flag and the not-ok ones in not_ok, up to max_not_ok; ok is no flag, null_only is the flag null alone, a point with no value and not a fault, and not ok is any other flag, so ok + null_only + not_ok_count = total), networks and devices (the same, plus disabled and each not-ok entry's name, type and enabled), totals (the n4_inventory totals of the same rows), capacity (resources: the Global Capacity counts and licence limits of the spy metrics page, unlimited true where the station shows no limit; recount: its recount times) and elapsed_ms. A section that fails is {error} and the others still answer. capacity is null with a capacity_note when the spy metrics page is unreachable or holds no Global Capacity table: never a guessed count. In a section, truncated means not_ok was cut at max_not_ok (not_ok_count is whole) and rows_truncated means the query hit max_rows, so the counts are lower bounds. A status the station did not answer counts under the flag unknown and as not ok, never as ok.

base.description: Subtree ORD of the point, network and device counts, default station:|slot:/

max_not_ok.description: Cap of the not-ok entries listed per section

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per request in seconds

write_tools.name: n4_create_component
write_tools.description: Add a component under parent_ord (optionally with a wire sheet position). Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

name.description: Requested slot name (the station may rename on collision)

wire_sheet.description: Optional {x, y, w} wire sheet annotation (integers; w defaults to 8)

proxy_ext.description: Optional driver proxy extension type spec (e.g. modbusCore:ModbusClientNumericProxyExt) to create a point with; configure its address afterwards with n4_set_slot

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_add_history
write_tools.description: Add one interval history extension per point, already configured: historyName (baja:Format pattern), interval (ms) and enabled, in one batch under one confirmation token (1 to 50 points). Refuses a point that already has a child named ext_name and, when the pattern only uses %name%/%parent...name% tokens, a history name that would repeat. Capacity stays at the extension default (500 records, Roll). Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

points.description: Point ORDs (1 to 50), each gets one extension

history_name.description: baja:Format pattern for the history name, unique per device, e.g. S%parent.parent.parent.name%_%parent.name%

interval_ms.description: Sampling interval in milliseconds (300000 is 5 minutes)

ext_name.description: Slot name of the extension under each point

enabled.description: Start collecting at once (true) or leave disabled

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_copy_component
write_tools.description: Copy one configured component (e.g. a Modbus device with its points and their addresses) under the same parent once per new name, in one batch under one confirmation token (1 to 30 copies). The copy holds the type, plain slots and child components up to 6 levels deep. Runtime slots are left out by flags read from the station's type definitions: a frozen slot declared readonly, transient or default-on-clone (e.g. status, health, out, read and write values) or made transient, and a dynamic slot flagged transient or remove-on-clone; flags an integrator set otherwise travel with the copy. The plan notes list each slot left out with its flags, calling out a readonly slot that holds a non-default value; actions, slots the station lists by name only and links are not copied either; a deeper source is refused. The read-back compares each copy's whole configured subtree with the plan. The source may carry station escapes (Numeric$20Writable40001); new names are plain. Change what differs per copy afterwards (e.g. deviceAddress with n4_set_slot). Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

parent_ord.description: ORD of the parent that holds the source and receives the copies

name.description: Slot name of the source child under parent_ord

new_names.description: Distinct plain slot names, one per copy (the station may rename on collision)

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_set_slot
write_tools.description: Set one slot to a value. Status slots are always written whole (value and status). A slot the station omits because it holds its type default is typed from the station's type definition (registry channel), so a default-valued property such as a history extension's enabled, historyName or interval can be set. A nested slot is a path from ord (grp/sp). Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

slot.description: Slot name, or a path of slot names separated by / for a nested slot; must be listed by the station or declared by its type

value.description: New value by value_type: a number (Double, StatusNumeric), true/false (Boolean, StatusBoolean), a string (String; Format takes its pattern, e.g. %parent.name%), or a whole number of milliseconds for RelTime (300000 is 5 minutes), a whole number for Integer (Java int range), or for Simple the encoded string of the type (a whole number is sent as its decimal string, e.g. a Modbus address 40014 on dataAddress/address) (an enum tag such as signedInteger or modbus, a Facets string such as units=u:celsius;...|precision=i:1, a LinearConversion scale;offset such as 0.1;0.0). A struct such as a Modbus FlexAddress is set through its child slots (dataAddress/addressFormat, dataAddress/address)

value_type.description: One of baja:Double, baja:Boolean, baja:String, baja:StatusNumeric, baja:StatusBoolean, baja:Format, baja:RelTime, baja:Integer, baja:Simple

simple_type.description: Only with baja:Simple: the type spec module:Type to send the value as when it replaces the slot's current type (e.g. driver:LinearConversion for a proxy conversion); default: the slot's own type

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_set_flags
write_tools.description: Set the flags of one slot of a component: either flags, the complete new set that replaces the current one (an empty string clears every flag), or add and/or remove, letters changed in the current set so the letters the slot already holds are kept. The plan shows the current and the requested flags with their names; the inverse restores the previous flags exactly, and the read-back loads the slot again and compares the two sets. Refused: both forms or neither, an unknown or repeated flag letter, a letter both added and removed, a slot the component does not have, a set equal to the current one, and a slot whose current flags cannot be read (not sent by the station and its type contract unreadable). Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

slot.description: Name of one slot of that component (a property, an action or a topic); not a path

flags.description: The complete new flag set as letters, each once, in any order; "" for no flags. Letters: r readonly, t transient, h hidden, s summary, a async, n no-run, d default-on-clone, c confirm-required, o operator, x execute-on-change, f fan-in, A no-audit, p composite, R remove-on-clone, m metadata, N non-critical, L link-target, 1 2 3 4 user-defined

add.description: Instead of flags: letters to add to the slot's current flags, each once (same letters as flags)

remove.description: Instead of flags: letters to remove from the slot's current flags, each once (same letters as flags)

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_invoke_action
write_tools.description: Invoke a control action. Only set, active, inactive, auto, and ping (a driver network, device or point device ext checks its device; no setting changes) are allowed in this version. Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

arg_type.description: baja:Double or baja:Boolean, only for set

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_create_link
write_tools.description: Create a link from a source slot to a target slot. Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_remove_component
write_tools.description: Remove the child `name` of parent_ord with its whole subtree. The plan snapshots the subtree to depth 3 (type, plain slots, wsAnnotation, links inside it) as the inverse; n4_rollback can re-create only that snapshot, not a full restore. Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

link_scan_ord.description: Optional wider ORD (inside the write scope) to scan for links from the subtree into components outside it

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_rollback
write_tools.description: Undo a journaled batch by running its recorded inverse through the same dry run / token pipeline, as a new batch linked to the original. Refuses unknown, already rolled back, in-doubt and other-station batches. Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

batch_id.description: batch_id returned by an earlier write

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_save_station
write_tools.description: Save the station (persist the running config to disk). The BOX reply proves nothing; persisted is true/false/unknown from config.bog when the server has --station-home for this station. Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)
